name: Attachment Style
subtitle: Attachment Style
instructions: Think about how you generally behave in your closest relationships, whether romantic or a very close friendship. Rate each statement from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree).

questions.text: Even when a relationship is going well, there are parts of yourself you tend to keep back rather than share openly.
In a stable relationship, you can find yourself paying attention to small changes in how the other person is acting toward you.
You find it relatively natural to let someone close see what's actually going on with you.
Your closest relationships tend to take up a fair amount of mental space, sometimes more than you'd like.
Even when things are going well with someone, you can find yourself pulling back a little without fully understanding why.
You have sometimes wondered whether the people you're closest to feel as strongly about you as you do about them.
When someone you're close to wants to spend more time together or share more of themselves, you can feel a quiet unease.
The thought of losing someone important to you tends to sit at the back of your mind more than you'd prefer.
Opening up and sharing the more private parts of yourself tends to happen slowly and carefully, if at all.
There are times when you've wanted more visible investment or enthusiasm from the person you were with.
You have had the experience of wanting to get closer to someone and then, once you did, feeling an urge to create some distance again.
At times, how much you wanted to connect with someone seemed to make them pull back from you.
When someone you care about tries to get closer emotionally, something in you can resist, even when you want the connection.
The idea of going through life without a stable, deep connection to someone is something you find genuinely unsettling.
Sharing your real thoughts with someone you trust doesn't feel like much of a risk.
There have been times when your need for closeness was more than what the other person seemed able or willing to match.
You tend to maintain a sense of your own independence in your relationships, keeping some emotional space.
Knowing regularly that you are wanted and valued in a relationship helps you feel more settled.
Getting close to someone and depending on them feels fairly natural rather than uncomfortable.
You have sometimes done something small to see how the other person would respond, just to get a sense of where you stood with them.
Asking for support from someone close, even when you genuinely need it, is something you tend to resist.
Worry about being left doesn't take up much space in your thinking when you're in a relationship.
You tend to feel most comfortable in relationships where both people keep a degree of their own separate life.
When a partner seems less present or engaged than usual, you tend to notice it fairly quickly and feel something about it.
There is very little you actively keep from someone you trust. You tend to share most of what's going on.
There have been relationships where you found yourself wanting more closeness than the other person seemed to want.
When something is weighing on you, your instinct is to bring it to your partner rather than work through it on your own.
Between relationships, you're aware of a low-level unease, like something important is absent.
Trusting someone enough to lean on them feels like a normal part of being close to them.
When a partner is busier or less available than usual, it tends to get under your skin a bit.
Asking someone close to you for comfort or help doesn't feel like weakness or an imposition.
When you need someone and they're not reachable, you feel it more acutely than you'd prefer.
When you're struggling, turning to the person you're with tends to be a natural first move.
When someone close to you is disappointed in you, or withdraws their warmth, you feel it quite strongly.
Your partner is usually among the first people you'd go to when something goes wrong.
When your partner's attention is elsewhere for a stretch of time, you tend to find it a little difficult to sit with.
